assessment: O-14-03 compares nutrition during gastric-cancer chemotherapy with S-1 and docetaxel. The PD occurrences are progressive cancer as a reason for treatment discontinuation.

O-30-06 relates serum IGF-1 to Hoehn and Yahr staging and UPDRS III in 99 Parkinson patients, with three-year staging examined in 42 earlier-stage patients. This is a biomarker study without a dietary intervention.

O-30-07 describes survival after oral intake ceased in 78 Parkinson, 13 PSP and 29 MSA patients. There were 44 tube-fed and 34 IV-only Parkinson patients. Tube-fed Parkinson median survival after oral cessation was 1.1 years (IQR 0.5–3.1). Formula ingredients were absent and the only significant between-group whole disease-duration result was in MSA. The authors cite a 2020 Parkinson predecessor. The center and years also overlap the 2018 JNS and 2019 JSPEN series; the 2022 PD subgroup counts differ.
O-38-01 is an esophageal-cancer case managed nutritionally through a passage obstruction during chemotherapy. PD is an oncology response assessment of progressive disease.
O-39-06 administers L-glutamine for poor nutrition in a postoperative cancer case. PD denotes pancreaticoduodenectomy.
O-46-02 compares nutritional indices and response to anti-PD-1 nivolumab in esophageal cancer.
O-52-08 investigates neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab in liver cancer. PD denotes progressive cancer.
O-54-04 compares liver-fibrosis indices after duodenum-preserving resection and pancreaticoduodenectomy, abbreviated PD.
O-62-03 tracks intake, body composition and grip strength in 35 pancreatic-resection patients. PD denotes pancreaticoduodenectomy.
O-62-04 studies time to nutritional recovery in the same 35-patient pancreatic-resection series as O-62-03. PD denotes pancreaticoduodenectomy.
O-62-06 discusses nutrition-team intervention and preoperative immunonutrition before pancreaticoduodenectomy in pancreatic cancer. PD refers to the surgical procedure.

O-67-02 combines electroconvulsive treatment, swallow therapy and a BCAA nutrition formula for an older man with Lewy body disease. Oral and then soft food became possible. The second patient who ate jelly had a psychiatric illness. The mention of an anti-Parkinson effect is background.

O-70-06 reviews 63 dysphagia patients receiving central venous ports, 27 with prior tube feeding. Parkinsonian syndrome is listed among underlying conditions without diagnosis-specific feeding or food results.
O-84-05 gives sulpiride for low appetite or depressed symptoms after pancreaticoduodenectomy, abbreviated PD.
O-86-02 describes two colorectal cancer cases treated with anamorelin. PD is progressive metastatic cancer in the treatment history.
O-07-2 compares preoperative zinc and biliary drainage in 77 pancreatic-surgery patients, with PD referring to 68 pancreaticoduodenectomies.

O-12-3 reports a 62-year-old woman with 13-year Parkinson disease, dyskinesia and rigidity, and BMI 11.1. After indirect calorimetry estimated 2,200 kcal/day resting expenditure, support was adjusted to about 2,000 kcal/day with oral and enteral intake. Weight reached 38 kg by discharge after 288 days. The report contains no named food or isolated symptom effect.

O-22-1 re-reports the 184-patient Utano Parkinson 3 mL jelly videofluoroscopy analysis from 2022 NHO. Motor scores associated with six of eight oral and four of four timing measures, and none of eight pharyngeal measures. Cohort also matches the 2018 aspiration prediction report; only one test consistency was assessed.

O-23-1 presented May 9, before June JNS. The same Utano cohort had 24 of 99 with glucose at or below 50 mg/dL in the final six months of life. Index-day energy was 538.3 ± 395 versus 911 ± 448 kcal/day. Mean event-to-death interval was 23.5 days. There are no ingredient data.
O-26-6 assesses short half-life proteins after pancreaticoduodenectomy, abbreviated PD, in 226 surgical patients.
O-40-3 studies nutrition-team intervention after pancreaticoduodenectomy for pancreatic-region malignancy. PD denotes the procedure.
O-44-7 describes a cancer case with erosion around an enteral stoma during steroids for immune-related liver injury. PD denotes cancer progression before nivolumab.
O-49-2 measures essential fatty acid fractions around pancreaticoduodenectomy, abbreviated PD. There are no Parkinson participants.

O-60-4 reports a 77-year-old woman diagnosed with parkinsonian syndrome who received multidisciplinary home oral-intake support after declining tube feeding. Intake eventually ceased and pneumonia-like fever occurred. No ingredient or texture is given.

O-61-3 demonstrates porridge jelly, udon, salmon, chicken and sweet-potato kinton made with an amylase-containing gelling agent for staff training. Outcomes are attendee responses without patient testing.
O-62-4 examines EPA and programmed death ligand 1 expression in human esophageal cancer cell lines.

O-64-4 reports a 71-year-old Parkinson patient with Duodopa PEG-J buried bumper and food residue leaking after replacement and meal resumption. The endpoint is a postoperative fistula, and the meal is unnamed.
O-07-1 examines EPA and anticancer drugs in human esophageal cancer cell lines, with PD-L1 expression as the endpoint.
O-08-1 associates muscle and adipose measures with hepatocellular-cancer drug outcomes. PD denotes progressive disease as a reason for therapy discontinuation.
O-27-2 studies postoperative sarcopenia and clinical factors in 50 pancreaticoduodenectomy patients. PD denotes the operation.
O-27-3 studies preoperative body composition and physical function as correlates of surgical complications in pancreatic cancer. PD denotes pancreaticoduodenectomy.

O-27-7 checks parkinsonian syndrome among comorbidities in 260 hip-fracture patients. Dementia and eGFR associated with low intake at discharge after adjustment. No Parkinson-specific or ingredient result is reported.

O-29-1 reports an 86-year-old Parkinson patient with dementia, worsening dysphagia and prior aspiration pneumonia who received PEG-J. Staff switched from pump to 90-minute manual delivery of Meibalance 500R. No dumping, diarrhea or malabsorption was reported. Post-switch swallowing and aspiration were not quantified.

O-31-3 treats pressure wounds in a bedbound Parkinson patient with bipolar disorder using protein, zinc and vitamin-enriched supplementation, wound care and pressure relief. Wound improvement followed combined care. The supplement product and Parkinson symptom change are unspecified.

O-35-5 reviews 305 aspiration-pneumonia admissions. Parkinson history is an extracted comorbidity. The adjusted associations with survival are aggregate and no food or Parkinson-specific outcome is given.
